findings.description: When the title has no recognised prefix, `want` is `undefined`. The loop then removes every `enhancement`, `bug`, `documentation`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore` or `perf` label on the PR, so a label a person added stays only until the next push or edit. Unprefixed titles are common here.
findings.body:
**A title with no prefix strips every type label, including ones added by hand**

[`.github/workflows/labeler.yml#L41-L51`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/2760a8f476f32ca8e9f8e1cded01fc81925d43e9/.github/workflows/labeler.yml#L41-L51)

If the title doesn't match the regex, `prefix` and `want` are both `undefined`. `name !== want` is then true for all seven type labels, so the loop removes each one the PR has. The workflow runs on `synchronize` and `edited`, so this happens on every push and every edit. The [header](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/2760a8f476f32ca8e9f8e1cded01fc81925d43e9/.github/workflows/labeler.yml#L1-L3) says "labels a person adds by hand stay", but a `bug` or `enhancement` someone puts on an unprefixed PR is gone after the next push.

Unprefixed titles are the norm here:
- `pup`'s merge gate titles its PRs from the task goal with no type prefix ([`src/core/merge-gate.service.ts`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/2760a8f476f32ca8e9f8e1cded01fc81925d43e9/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2918)).
- The last four squash merges on `main` have no prefix (#223, #218, #213, #206).

A title with no prefix says nothing about the type. Leave the type labels alone in that case and only swap them when the title names a type.

findings.description: The script takes `have` from `context.payload.pull_request.labels`, which is the label set when the event fired. Runs for the same PR also execute in parallel. So a title edit made soon after opening leaves two type labels, and an edit plus a push close together makes `removeLabel` fail with a 404.

`TYPES[prefix]` also matches keys inherited from `Object.prototype`. A title like `constructor: x` or `toString: x` makes `want` a function, which strips every type label and then fails the job on `addLabels`. Use `Object.hasOwn(TYPES, prefix) ? TYPES[prefix] : undefined`.
`area/tooling` covers `.claude/**`, `.github/**` and `scripts/**` but not `tools/**`. A PR that only touches `tools/review`, the CI review tooling, gets no area label.

`pull_request_target` reads `.github/labeler.yml` from the base branch, which won't have it until this PR merges. On this PR the labeler step is likely to fail, and the title-prefix step after it won't run. This is a one-time effect.

process_issues.description: Every Bash call failed in the sandbox with 'apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/setgroups (nested userns is capability-restricted; caller must provide CAP_SYS_ADMIN): Permission denied'. So `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff` and `git diff` were all unavailable. The changed-file list was inferred from the commit subject and from files in the repo (.github/workflows/labeler.yml, .github/labeler.yml), and their full contents were reviewed as added. No changed line was checked for provenance against the real diff.

Could not read the PR body, comments or closing issues, so the steering brief and spec sources were empty and review-spec did not run. The second freshness check (HEAD vs headRefOid) also could not run. HEAD was read from .git/refs as 2760a8f476f32ca8e9f8e1cded01fc81925d43e9.

After the config restore, .claude/agents/architecture-explainer.md shows as modified, so the PR probably touches it. Its PR copy is not under .claude-pr/, so that file was not reviewed. review-maintainability was skipped because the logic change is small: two YAML files.
